commonInstruction: Decide the current scenario at the stated boundary from the supplied fixed source and accepted policy. Treat listed premises as question assumptions at the named entry, not as source or deployment proof. Trace the decisive authorization control and protected effect with exact supplied-source locations. Answer every explicitly requested counterfactual branch separately, identifying its changed assumptions and any decisive unknown. Include only the response details requested below. Do not execute the target, infer missing deployment facts, or consult later versions.

cases.selection: AH exposed mechanism: target-specific write authorization
premises: At POST /process/file the verified non-admin owns the supplied file but has no ownership or write grant on the existing caller-selected destination collection.
requiredResponseDetails: Identify the destination write sink and distinguish source-file ownership from destination write permission.

cases.selection: AH exposed mechanism: policy label direction
premises: At POST /process/text the verified non-admin selects an existing collection without ownership or a write grant and supplies the text.
requiredResponseDetails: Trace the caller-side and shared authorization controls before the text write sink.

cases.selection: AH exposed mechanism: requested branches and deployment unknown
premises: The caller is unauthenticated outside the trusted identity proxy and asks whether an actual reachable deployment permits impersonation via a client-supplied trusted-email header.
requiredResponseDetails: Identify the configuration and header-to-identity path, applicable denial/status behavior when source shows it, and the minimum missing facts for the actual deployment.

cases.selection: AH exposed mechanism: stated handler-entry premise
premises: At entry to read_item, current_user is the authenticated active superuser described by this task, and the existing item's owner differs from that caller.
requiredResponseDetails: Separate this handler-entry conclusion from any claim that the supplied crop proves the upstream CurrentUser binding.

cases.selection: AH exposed mechanism: repository permission and requested branches
premises: At the named POST handler the caller is authenticated, token issue-write scope is present, the issue and requested assignee exist, and repository issue-write permission is absent.
requiredResponseDetails: Distinguish token scope from repository issue-write permission and state whether each path reaches assignee resolution and mutation.

cases.selection: AH exposed mechanism: route-level role and policy label direction
premises: At the named PUT route the authenticated caller has full token scope and issue-write permission but neither repository-admin nor site-admin status; the issue exists and is unlocked.
requiredResponseDetails: Trace the route and handler gates in order and identify whether the lock mutation is reached.

cases.selection: declared-scenario-variation: same source, supplied-path rather than handler-entry binding
premises: The external caller claims to be an authenticated active superuser and requests another user's existing item; the supplied handler crop alone does not assert what current_user the dependency injects.
requiredResponseDetails: Distinguish what the handler proves conditionally from what the supplied path proves about the actual caller-to-current_user binding.

cases.selection: declared-scenario-variation: same source, self relation instead of other-user relation
premises: At GetRepoPermissions the authenticated repository-read collaborator is neither a site nor repository administrator, and the queried username is the caller's own existing username.
requiredResponseDetails: Explain the self-query branch and distinguish it from the other-user role check.

sourceAccess: Only the fixed supplied source crop and accepted policy for each case. No held-out or target execution.
publicParagraphRule: The commonInstruction and each case's boundary, premises, requestedBranches, and requiredResponseDetails are rendered verbatim once in all four arm prompts; semantic equivalents in the input representation do not replace this paragraph.
